item.title: Julia cells
item.description:
A ```julia block is a Julia cell (parsed since go-notebook v0.6.0, run in go-notebook v0.18.0; on go-embedded-julia v0.17.0 since v0.19.0). go-embedded-julia is the pure-Go Julia these cells run on: its parser for the names and the syntax errors, its interpreter (v0.17.0) for the running. No external julia is started.

Running

The cells of a notebook share one Julia kernel, in the worker. A global, a function or a struct a cell defines is there in the next cell; what a cell prints is its own output, and the value of its last expression is shown as the Julia REPL shows it, unless it is nothing or the cell ends in a semicolon.

```julia
square(x) = x^2
total = sum(square(i) for i in 1:4)
```

```julia
println("total = ", total)
total + 1
```
$ notebook run julia.md
── cell 0 (line 4, ran in 1.102209s)
 30
── cell 1 (line 9, ran in 1.478ms)
 total = 30
 31

(A real transcript, from the change that became go-notebook v0.18.0, on an Apple M4 Max; the first cell pays the kernel’s cold start.)

An exception fails the cell with julia’s text of it after ERROR:, after the output the cell wrote before it; the cells that read it do not run, and the kernel keeps what it had.

The image. The kernel boots from go-embedded-julia’s prebuilt Base image, which is not part of the module. The first Julia cell a worker runs fetches the image of release v0.17.0 and loads it only if its SHA-256 is the one go-notebook pins (d243d2b748afb7d331227195d835357b6502184bedcdc4bcc296854276c2f6ec); the verified file is kept in your user cache directory (go-embedded-julia/images) and checked again each time. The fetch is bounded to five minutes and tried once. The cold start is about a second. On a machine that is offline and has no cached image every Julia cell of the run fails at once with the Julia kernel could not start, and the other cells run.

Limits. A notebook may come from anyone, so each cell is bounded, as an R cell is: 30 seconds, 50 million statements, a memory budget of 512 MiB, and 16 MiB of output per stream. The memory budget counts the elements of the arrays and dictionary tables a cell allocates, in total and garbage included, at 16 bytes each. It is a floor, not the heap: a boxed value costs more, strings are not counted, and one array may not have more than 2^24 elements whatever the budget. A cell over a limit is stopped and says which, in the kernel’s words; --timeout and --memory still apply to the worker. The kernel is sandboxed: its file system holds julia’s own tree and its environment is empty.

Soft scope. As in IJulia, a loop at the top level that updates a global works: s=0; for i in 1:10; s+=i; end gives 55. A MethodError shows Julia’s own text (no method matching, closest candidates).

Known limitations (go-embedded-julia v0.17.0):

  • On the Base image, a Float64 A * x needs BLAS (#67), and a non-ASCII uppercase needs utf8proc (#65).
  • Get refuses an n×0 matrix (#76).
  • A process loads one image release (#49).

Parsing and names

The names below are the same whether a cell runs or not.

Parsing. A Julia cell is parsed by go-embedded-julia’s port of JuliaSyntax, the parser julia 1.12 ships, which gives the same Expr trees as julia on its whole test corpus. A syntax error is reported at the notebook’s line and column, with julia’s own message:

```julia
y = 2
x = (1,
```
$ notebook run broken.md
── cell 0 (line 4, not run)
 error: 5:8: cell 0: syntax error: Expected `)` or `,`
notebook: 1 cell(s) failed

The parse is bounded — 4 MiB per cell, a nesting depth of 1000 — so a notebook from anyone cannot make it run long or exhaust memory; a cell over the limits fails with a message saying so.

Names. A Julia cell joins the rules of cells and the dependency graph: one definition per name, no assignment to another cell’s variable, a name starting with _ kept in its cell. Its names follow Julia’s own scope rules for an interactive context, as written in Scope of Variables (Julia manual, 1.12):

Construct In the notebook
x = 1, a, b = …, x::Int = 1, global x = 1 at the top level, or in if/begin there defines the variable
f(x) = …, function f … end, macro m … end (as @m) defines a function or macro
const C = …, struct S, abstract type, primitive type, module M defines a constant or type
using A, using A: x, y, import A.B, import A as B defines what it binds (A; x and y; B)
function, macro and struct bodies, let, do, ->, comprehensions and generators hard scopes: an assignment there makes a local
for, while, try at the top level soft scopes: an assignment there to an existing global assigns it (as in the REPL and IJulia); otherwise it makes a local of the loop
a name read before the cell assigns it, in any scope where no local binds it a use: the cell depends on the cell that defines it

These rules are checked against julia itself: 61 cells, from each kind of definition to keyword defaults, where bounds and nested generators, are lowered by julia 1.12.6 (through REPL.softscope, the soft-scope rule of the REPL), and the globals julia declares and reads are the names go-notebook finds.

Across languages. Since go-notebook v0.19.0, Julia variables cross with Go cells in both directions (Kernel.Get/Set), and Julia is no longer Isolated: a Go cell that reads a Julia name depends on the Julia cell. This breaks v0.18.0, where Julia variables stayed in Julia.

  • Types that cross: Int64, Float64 (bits kept, NaN payloads and -0.0 included), Bool, String, and Vector and Matrix of Float64 or Int64 (column-major). Go int and []int cross as Int64.
  • A Julia value of another type stays in Julia; the Go cell that reads it is deferred, naming the type.
  • A Go value Julia cannot take fails the Julia cell that reads it.
  • Inputs are measured before any copy: one array has at most 2^24 elements, and a cell’s inputs together are at most its memory limit. A cell can therefore hold up to twice its limit: its inputs plus its own allocations.

Between Julia cells every name is shared. The HTML page shows a Julia cell highlighted with go-rouge’s julia lexer.

In the browser

The playground does not run Julia cells: its WebAssembly core parses and checks them, the cell’s badge reads Julia — not runnable yet, and the cell says Julia cells run in go-notebook, not yet in the browser. The page treats Julia as check-only by language, so a Julia cell never reaches its Go evaluator. Running them there is a separate question, pending with go-embedded-julia.

Try the Julia example notebook there for the checks; notebook run and notebook serve run the cells.
